notes: Kinetic escalation on both sides, resolved crew question, flat oil. Tue 17 Nov: after Iran's third drone attack on the Sheikh Isa radar in Bahrain (CENTCOM: intercepted, no damage, Iran's hit claim 'FALSE'), US fighter jets struck an IRGC missile launch site on Qeshm Island with precision munitions - a US military official confirmed it ~19:27Z as 'self-defense... in response to IRGC aggression targeting US personnel and assets'; Fars reported the explosion ~13:33Z; Iran says no damage (Nariman air-defence launcher hit per Iranian media). This is the third confirmed Qeshm strike of November (2 and 6 Nov already recorded) and Air & Space Forces says the US has run unannounced limited strikes since September - it is a US strike on Iran by the brief's definition, at the established tit-for-tat scale. Iran's regular army answered overnight: Kuwait's General Staff was intercepting hostile drones from ~21:39Z, and at 04:26Z 18 Nov the army claimed strikes on Patriot batteries and launch platforms at Ali Al-Salem - the first claimed Iranian attack on Kuwait in this phase; Bahrain reports a fourth round intercepted; Kuwait invokes Article 51 and UNSCR 2817; GCC, UAE, Qatar and Saudi condemn. Maritime: the 11-17 'crew unaccounted for' flag on TARA GAS resolves to crew abandoned ship, 24 accounted for (21 evacuated at Khasab, 2 hospitalised) and ONE Indian seafarer MISSING with SAR ongoing (India MEA/Sonowal; Oman 18 Nov: 24 evacuated, one still missing, fire still burning) - not a confirmed death. Separately ADNOC L&S says one of its ships (unnamed) was attacked 'Tuesday evening' while transiting the Strait: 1 missing, 11 injured, rest evacuated - apparently a second hull (Tara Gas is Matrix Maritime-managed), unconfirmed; no new UKMTO warning number surfaced. Two missing seafarers is the heaviest confirmed human toll so far; no sinking or death confirmed; Iran's claims (mine 'heavily damaged' tanker, 'third tanker', 'LNG ship and two tankers on fire') remain unverified. hormuz.now 17 Nov 21:19Z: 7d avg 6.6/day (46/7d, 8% of 84.8), 16 Nov full day 6, 17 Nov 3 partial, tankers 14/7d (2.0/day, 4%), 368 tankers/35 VLCC visible; PortWatch tanker tonnage 0.8% of normal to 15 Nov; straits.live unreachable. Oil: Brent Jan-27 settled 93.14 (+0.70, +0.76%), WTI Dec-26 86.01 (+0.29) after a $91.26-94.08 swing on the strike exchange; Bloomberg: prompt backwardation ~2.80 vs >3 a month ago; Saudi/UAE OSPs cut; DTN: Hormuz crude transits 'recovered to pre-war 13.5 mb/d', Gulf exports incl. pipeline ~18.5 mb/d, Iraq Kirkuk-Ceyhan restart 120 kb/d; API crude +5.28 mb; Wed Asia Brent 92.61 at 07:30 GMT. Houthis claim East-West pipeline pumping stations 8/9 and declare Bab el-Mandeb theirs; Saudi coalition hits 60 targets. Politics: Qatar says mediation continues, met the Iranian side 17 Nov, escalation an 'extremely grave danger' to a deal, Al Ansari 'narrowing the gap' - but RFE/RL finds no public direct US-Iran channel and an Iranian MP accuses Qatar of talking up progress for markets; Trump (Manila) takes the dirty-bomb report 'very seriously', WH says no credible threat, Araghchi 'RUBBISH'; 18 Nov Trump to CNBC 'doing very well in Iran', departs for Shenzhen (Iran on agenda per WH). No Witkoff, IAEA, OFAC, EU Defence FAC/Aspides, or Israel-specific tell in gate (CENTCOM chief visiting Israel 18 Nov). Net: Strait closed, no deal, a confirmed limited US strike on Iran answered by a new front (Kuwait), two seafarers missing, and an oil market that closed +0.76% and narrowed its prompt spread.

items.name: US fighter jets strike an IRGC missile launch site on Qeshm Island 'in self-defense' (US military official, ~19:27Z 17 Nov) after Iran's third drone attack on the Bahrain radar; CENTCOM calls Iran's Bahrain hit claim 'FALSE'; Iran says no damage, Tasnim 'several projectiles', Nariman launcher hit
items.headline: US confirms it struck IRGC missile launch site on Iran's Qeshm Island / US jets strike IRGC missile launch site on Iran's Qeshm Island in 'self-defence'
items.claim: A US military official said US fighter aircraft struck an IRGC missile launch site on Qeshm Island with precision munitions: 'The strike was in response to IRGC aggression targeting US personnel and assets'; 'US Central Command remains highly vigilant and fully postured to protect Americans across the region.' CENTCOM separately said the Iranian one-way drones aimed at Isa Air Base, Bahrain 'were intercepted without any damage to US equipment or injury to American personnel' and labelled the IRGC's radar-hit claim 'FALSE' (~12:41Z). Fars reported an explosion on Qeshm ~13:33Z; a provincial official said no damage to residential or vital infrastructure; Iranian media said an air-defence missile launcher at Nariman was hit. Air & Space Forces: not the first post-ceasefire strike - the US has conducted a series of limited, unannounced strikes since early September; Iran claims a US drone (LUCAS per Iran International / MQ-1 per ASF) downed over the Strait, unverified.
items.source: Iran International 17 Nov 19:27Z; The National 17 Nov 21:28Z; Air & Space Forces 17 Nov 21:34Z; CBS live 17 Nov 14:38 ET; Khaleej Times live 17 Nov 19:57 and 23:27 UAE; DTN 17 Nov
items.note: A US kinetic strike on Iranian territory, publicly confirmed by a US official the same day - the third confirmed Qeshm strike of November (2 Nov 'defensive', 6 Nov 'minor strikes', both already recorded) and framed as limited/self-defence rather than a campaign; no Trump/Hegseth statement on it found. Iran's army answered within hours with drones at Ali Al-Salem, Kuwait (see hit). Oil's $3 intraday swing on the exchange faded to +0.76%. Reads as the brief's 'US strike on Iran' category but at the tit-for-tat scale the series has carried since September - the scorer decides.

items.name: Iran's army says its drones struck Patriot batteries and drone/missile launch platforms at Ali Al-Salem Air Base, Kuwait (~04:26Z 18 Nov) in retaliation for Qeshm; Kuwait's General Staff intercepting 'hostile' drones from ~21:39Z 17 Nov; Kuwait invokes UN Charter Art. 51 and UNSCR 2817; GCC, UAE, Qatar, Saudi condemn
items.headline: Iran's army says drones targeted US systems at Kuwait air base / Gulf Crisis Deepens: Iran Targets Bahrain, ADNOC Vessel Attacked, US Responds with Strikes
items.claim: Kuwait's army said from ~01:39 UAE (21:39Z 17 Nov) that its air defences were intercepting hostile drones and that explosions residents heard were interceptions (CBS 18:59 ET: no claim of responsibility at the time). At 08:26 UAE 18 Nov Iran's army said its 'combat attack drones' targeted Patriot air-defence systems and 'platforms used to launch drones and missiles' at Ali Al-Salem, warning 'any threat against the Islamic Republic of Iran will receive a decisive and crushing response' and framing it as retaliation for the 17 Nov Qeshm strike. Kuwait's foreign ministry (10:50 UAE) condemned 'repeated Iranian drone attacks' as violations of UNSCR 2817 and invoked the right to self-defence under Article 51; the GCC Secretary-General (04:34 and 14:11 UAE), UAE (11:42), Qatar (07:47Z) and Saudi Arabia condemned the Bahrain and Kuwait attacks; the GCC urged UNSC action. No CENTCOM statement on Kuwait at run time; no damage or casualties confirmed.
items.source: Gulf News live 18 Nov (01:39, 06:54, 08:26, 10:50, 11:42, 14:11 UAE); houseofsaud 18 Nov 07:48Z; Iran International live 18 Nov 06:44Z and 07:47Z; CBS live 17 Nov 18:59 ET; Tasnim/Anadolu/MEE relays (not fetched)
items.note: Widening of Iran's Gulf-host-state campaign from Bahrain (three attacks, 13-17 Nov) to Kuwait - the first claimed Iranian strike on Kuwait in this phase - and the first explicitly attributed to the regular army rather than the IRGC. Bahrain Defence Force (06:54 UAE 18 Nov) says it intercepted further Iranian strikes overnight, a fourth round. Saudi early-warning alerts for Jazan/Najran/Khamis Mushait 18 Nov (all-clear 13:23 UAE). Kuwait's Article 51 language is a legal predicate for Gulf self-defence/collective action; Mecca Joint Defence Pact meeting noted (Khaleej 18:40 UAE 17 Nov, no detail).

items.name: TARA GAS resolution: crew abandoned ship after the second strike; India MEA - 21 of 24 Indians evacuated at Khasab, 2 hospitalised, 1 seafarer missing; Oman 18 Nov - 24 evacuated, 1 still missing, firefighting ongoing; separately ADNOC L&S says one of its ships was attacked 'Tuesday evening' - 1 missing, 11 injured
items.headline: Second Strike on LPG Tanker in Strait of Hormuz Leaves One Missing, Two Injured / UAE's ADNOC L&S Says One Crew Member Missing After Attack on Its Vessel in Hormuz
items.claim: gCaptain (17 Nov 15:00Z): after UKMTO's Tuesday update that a maritime security agency reported a second strike and fire on the Khasab tanker with crew whereabouts unaccounted, India's Sonowal identified TARA GAS, confirmed the second attack and the crew's abandonment of the vessel: '24 crew members have been safely accounted for, one Indian seafarer remains missing'; India's MEA: 21 of 24 Indian nationals evacuated ashore at Khasab, two hospitalised; Oman's emergency committee (18 Nov ~09:08Z): 24 evacuated from the burning tanker off Musandam, one still missing. ADNOC L&S (18 Nov, Reuters/The National/Arab Times): one of its ships was attacked while transiting the Strait on Tuesday evening; 'one crew member remains unaccounted for, with search and rescue operations ongoing'; 11 injured 'receiving medical care where required', all others evacuated; ADNOC 'reiterates the importance of protecting seafarers and safeguarding freedom of navigation'. The ADNOC vessel is unnamed; no source links it to TARA GAS.
items.source: gCaptain 17 Nov 07:00 PST and 18 Nov 01:04 PST; The National 18 Nov 06:41Z; Arab Times 18 Nov 10:32+03; Gulf News live 18 Nov 10:45 and 13:08 UAE; Khaleej Times live 17 Nov 15:15 and 19:11 UAE; nriaffairs; shipuniverse; econotimes (not fetched)
items.note: Resolves the 11-17 'crew unaccounted for' flag: not a confirmed loss of life - one Indian seafarer missing with SAR ongoing, two injured. The ADNOC L&S report adds a second missing seafarer and 11 injured on what appears to be a different hull (ADNOC-operated vs Matrix Maritime-managed Tara Gas) attacked the same evening; the 15 Nov Al Dhannah (ADNOC-linked, steering gear) is a separate, earlier incident. Two missing seafarers across two ships is the heaviest confirmed human toll of the standoff; a body recovery or owner confirmation of death would convert this to a hard event. Attribution: press headlines say Iran; UKMTO/owners do not attribute.

items.name: Qatar: US-Iran mediation 'continues', meeting with the Iranian side 17 Nov, escalation an 'extremely grave danger' to a deal; Al Ansari - 'narrowing the gap between proposals'; Iranian MP Mahmoudi (18 Nov) accuses Qatar of talking up progress to calm markets; RFE/RL: no publicly known direct Washington-Tehran Hormuz channel
items.headline: Qatar to hold meeting with Iran as Doha warns regional escalation threatens diplomatic efforts (Doha News, unreachable) / CBS live 17 Nov 13:52 ET
items.claim: CBS (17 Nov 06:04 and 13:52 ET): Qatar urged 'all parties' to exercise restraint and avoid escalation that could undermine negotiations, then said US-Iran mediation continues with a meeting with the Iranian side planned later Tuesday, warning that escalation poses an 'extremely grave danger' to a deal. houseofsaud (18 Nov 03:54Z) relays Al Ansari via RFE/RL describing the mediation as 'narrowing the gap between proposals' and RFE/RL's finding that no publicly known diplomatic channel between Washington and Tehran on Hormuz currently exists; Turkey has confirmed a second 'R-4' meeting in Europe (undated). Iran International (18 Nov 07:21Z): lawmaker Morteza Mahmoudi accused Qatar of portraying Iran-US talks as advancing to calm markets while serving US policy goals. Khaleej: Pakistan's army chief met Araghchi (12:43 UAE 17 Nov); UAE and Qatari FMs discussed developments (21:02 UAE).
items.source: CBS live 17 Nov; houseofsaud 18 Nov 03:54Z (RFE/RL relay); Iran International live 18 Nov 07:21Z; Khaleej Times live 17 Nov
items.note: The Qatar channel is live and meeting Iranians the same day as the Qeshm strike and the Bahrain attack, but with no US-side meeting reported and Tehran's own parliamentarians disputing Qatar's framing. Araghchi's Muscat meeting (17 Nov, no agreement) already recorded 11-17; the ONA 'no Hormuz agreement' line restated by houseofsaud. No Witkoff item in gate. Doha News primary unreachable (client_error).

items.name: Trump (Manila, ~12:15Z 17 Nov): takes the reported Iranian dirty-bomb plot 'very seriously', Iran would 'pay a heavy price'; WH's Bis: no credible threats to the homeland, planning is Iran 'giving itself options'; Araghchi calls the reports 'RUBBISH', Baghaei 'baseless'; 18 Nov to CNBC: 'We are looking into it. We are doing very well in Iran'
items.headline: CBS live 17 Nov 07:15 ET / The National 17 Nov / houseofsaud 18 Nov
items.claim: Trump, asked about the CNN report of Iranian option-building for a radiological or chemical attack on Washington, said he takes it 'very seriously' and warned Iran would pay a heavy price if it happened; White House spokesperson Lauren Bis said there were no credible threats to the homeland and the earlier WH line (02:33 ET) was that Iran's planning was an effort to 'give itself options'. Baghaei (08:18 ET) dismissed the report as baseless; Araghchi (11:46 ET) called the dirty-bomb and 'missile-under-dam' reports 'RUBBISH' and blamed Israel; Iran's deputy FM rejected it again at 00:30 UAE 18 Nov. On 18 Nov in Manila Trump told CNBC 'We are looking into it. We are doing very well in Iran.' Trump flies to China 18 Nov for the 19 Nov Shenzhen trilateral; the WH says he will raise Iran, Trump said Iran would come up 'a little bit' (HNGN 17 Nov 08:17 EST).
items.source: CBS live 17 Nov 02:33, 07:15, 08:18, 11:46 ET; The National 17 Nov 21:28Z; houseofsaud 18 Nov 07:48Z (CNBC relay); HNGN 17 Nov 08:17 EST; Fox live 18 Nov 02:35 EST
items.note: Only Trump statements dated in gate; no statement from him on the Qeshm strike, the Bahrain/Kuwait attacks or the missing seafarers surfaced. 'Doing very well' + 'very seriously' on the plot is consistent with the 15 Nov 'status quo' posture. Rubio: call with Bahrain's FM after the attack (Khaleej 07:22 UAE 17 Nov), no quote in gate. CENTCOM chief visiting Israel 18 Nov (Gulf News 13:09 UAE). Shenzhen pre-read unchanged from 11-16/11-17 (Iran on agenda per US officials; Beijing names only 'peace and strategic stability').

items.name: Houthis claim drone strikes on Saudi East-West pipeline pumping stations 8 and 9 (~18:20Z 17 Nov) and declare Bab el-Mandeb 'safer now' under Houthi control; Saudi-led coalition intercepts drones/cruise missile at Riyadh on a fourth straight day and hits 60 Houthi targets 18 Nov; Iraq restarts Kirkuk-Ceyhan exports at 120 kb/d
items.headline: CBS live 17 Nov 08:59, 12:46, 13:20, 14:17 ET; Khaleej Times live 17 Nov 22:18 UAE; Gulf News live 18 Nov 07:35, 09:55 UAE
items.claim: Houthi spokesman Saree said Bab el-Mandeb lanes are 'safer now' after the Houthis took control of the Yemeni coast there (after Saudi-led/Southern forces withdrew); the Houthis then claimed drone strikes on East-West pipeline pumping stations 9 and 8 feeding Yanbu (Saudi Arabia had not confirmed damage; Khaleej 22:18 UAE: drones launched toward the pipeline). The Saudi-led coalition shot down a Houthi drone near Riyadh (fourth straight day), a cruise missile aimed at Riyadh on 18 Nov, and said it destroyed 60 Houthi targets across Sanaa, Hodeidah, Saada and Amran. Separately Iraq's oil minister said crude pumping to Turkey via Kirkuk-Ceyhan resumed at 120 kb/d, planned to ~500 kb/d.
items.source: CBS live 17 Nov; Khaleej Times live 17 Nov; Gulf News live 18 Nov; DTN 17 Nov (pipeline/Bab el-Mandeb as price drivers)
items.note: Bypass-route risk: the East-West pipeline to Yanbu is the main Hormuz bypass the oil market is pricing (DTN 'Gulf exports incl. diverted pipeline ~18.5 mb/d'); Houthi claims on its pumping stations are unconfirmed and were already a theme 15 Nov (recorded 11-16) - the 17 Nov claims on stations 8/9 and the Bab el-Mandeb control statement are new. Kirkuk-Ceyhan restart is a bearish supply item recorded here for the O panel context.

items.name: Oil steadies +0.76% through a US-Iran strike exchange: DTN says Hormuz crude transits 'recovered to pre-war 13.5 mb/d' and Gulf exports incl. diverted pipeline ~18.5 mb/d; Bloomberg - Brent prompt backwardation ~$2.80 vs >$3 a month ago; API crude +5.3 mb; Saudi/UAE OSPs cut
items.headline: Crude Steadies on Mideast Flare Ups; Refined Products Slip / Oil Prices Swing as Gulf Attacks Continue
items.claim: DTN (17 Nov 2:50pm CST): Brent Jan 93.14 (+0.70) and WTI Dec 86.01 (+0.29) after a ~$3 range, supported by the third Bahrain drone attack, the Qeshm strike, the UKMTO alert and Houthi pipeline claims, capped by Vance's 'no prolonged war', Hormuz crude transits recovered to pre-war levels of 13.5 mb/d, Gulf exports incl. diverted pipeline volumes near 18.5 mb/d, Iraq's Kirkuk-Ceyhan restart, OPEC's October data (Iraq above pre-war, Saudi >10.5 mb/d) and US IP -0.4%. Bloomberg via Rigzone: Brent's prompt spread around $2.80 backwardation vs more than $3 a month ago; Saudi and UAE OSPs cut; US retail diesel below $6 for the first time since early September; TD's McKay expects risk premium to return 'as tensions grow'. API after the close: crude +5.28 mb, gasoline +5.12 mb. Wed Asia Brent 92.61.
items.source: DTN 17 Nov 2:50pm CST; Bloomberg via Rigzone 17 Nov 15:53 EST; financefeeds 18 Nov 07:30 GMT; cappnotes 17 Nov
items.note: Oil-market-structure headline for the O panel: a confirmed US strike on Iran plus two ships with missing crew produced a +0.76% close and a narrowing prompt spread - the market is pricing bypass volumes and the surplus over Hormuz risk. DTN's '13.5 mb/d transits recovered to pre-war' conflicts with hormuz.now's 8% of baseline, Kpler's 48% and PortWatch's 0.8% tanker tonnage - different methods/denominators, flagged, not reconciled.
